items.title: 员工每月烧掉数千美元 Token，Salesforce“吃不消了”拟设 AI 使用预算

items.title: 微软推出 Copilot Today：打工人的“全自动 AI 助理”，替你排好一天工作
items.description: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，在昨日（11 月 17 日）召开的 Ignite 2026 大会上，微软推出全新 Copilot Today 功能， 目标把 AI 助手从“你问、它答”推进到“它先看、再帮你准备”的工作模式。 该功能整合在 Microsoft Copilot 应用和 Outlook 中，可将邮件、日历、Teams 聊天、会议和任务等信息汇总为统一的工作中心。 Today 由两部分组成：Today Brief 提供个性化晨间简报，列出当天最重要的任务；Today Feed 则会随新邮件、新消息和新日程不断刷新，让用户不必在多个应用之间来回查找。IT之家附上相关截图如下： 在实际落地场景上，对于普通职场用户而言，早晨打开电脑后，可能不再需要先翻邮件、查日历、翻聊天记录，会直接看到一个由 AI 整理的“今日待办”。 Copilot Today 目前仅以 Frontier 私有预览版面向部分用户开放，覆盖 Microsoft Copilot 应用和 Outlook。不过，该功能也带来新的隐私与注意力问题：AI 需要读取大量工作数据，才能判断哪些事情值得优先处理。

items.title: 微软 Office 翻开新篇章：Copilot AI 应用集成 Word 等唱主角
items.description: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，在昨日（11 月 17 日）召开的 Ignite 2026 大会上，微软官宣 Office 的“新篇章”，将办公软件从传统的文档、表格与演示工具， 进一步转向由 AI 智能体协同完成工作的“智能办公系统”。 IT之家曾于 10 月报道， 微软逆转办公 AI 策略 ，此前主要将 Copilot 嵌入到 Office 应用中， 而现在围绕着新款 Copilot 应用，集成完整的 Word、Excel 和 PowerPoint 创建、编辑与协作体验。 在本次活动中，微软宣布 Copilot 已正式上线 Office 支持，用户只需用自然语言提出需求，Copilot 便可在 Word、PowerPoint、Excel 中生成文档，并在聊天窗口旁打开。微软表示用户既能手动修改，也可继续让 AI 调整。所有内容保存在 OneDrive，并受企业安全与合规策略约束。 微软还推出面向销售的 Copilot for Sales Frontier 公开版，可通过插件和技能连接 CRM，以及 Zendesk、HubSpot、Notion、DocuSign、ZoomInfo

items.title: 微软拟升级 Copilot，要给你的 Win11 电脑“看病”

items.title: 苹果订阅版 Final Cut Pro 加入 MotionVFX，视频特效更省事
items.description: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，科技媒体 MacRumors 昨日（11 月 17 日）发布博文， 报道称苹果面向 Apple 创作坊（Apple Creator Studio）用户，升级视频剪辑软件 Final Cut Pro，新增集成 MotionVFX 功能。 IT之家曾于今年 3 月报道， 苹果收购 Final Cut Pro 插件公司 MotionVFX ，在本次更新后，该公司的素材库被直接纳入 FCP，涵盖模板、标题、主题、特效、版式和转场等创作者常用资源。 功能方面，用户可将 MotionVFX 图形和特效直接拖入视频时间轴，也能在场景中添加 3D 标题和图形。新功能支持将 3D 元素放置在移动表面，或依据镜头运动匹配自然景深，从而提升视频的立体感与真实感。 新版还改进遮罩功能，创作者可以更快为视频中的人物或物体添加轮廓、强调效果和运动轨迹；静态照片、插画还可被转换为动画。 苹果同时新增“内容中心”（Content Hub），提供素材视频、照片、图形和背景。创作者还能通过文字描述在 FCP 内生成图像，并继续编辑。项目中的任意图像可打开至 Pixelmator Pro

items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang , the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations. “We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.” The company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. items.description: Nvidia's interim CEO says the company is done selling chips to China. How much will that cost?
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country. China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies , export control compliance, and global trade risks. Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff. The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.” Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely. items.description: The SEC is opening a probe into Nvidia following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, reports The Wall Street Journal.
items.author: Rebecca Bellan
items.content: The Securities and Exchange Commission is opening a civil probe into Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, according to The Wall Street Journal . The investigation adds to Nvidia’s stack of drama after CEO Jensen Huang resigned following news of his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed. The Commerce Department has been investigating Megaspeed since late 2024 under suspicion that the company diverted some of its Nvidia chips to China, which would violate U.S. export laws. Congress has also demanded that Huang answer questions about his affair and how it might have affected his stance that export restrictions should be loosened. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent put it more bluntly over the weekend, accusing Nvidia of knowingly selling powerful chips to China to “goose their revenues and their earnings.” The news of the SEC probe also comes as Nvidia reports earnings to a market that has seen its stock fall more than 10% since Huang departed. items.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it’s not having one
items.description: With tech outages seemingly everywhere, Google took the unusual step of announcing that Gmail is working just fine, actually.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: Was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages? The company took to X on Tuesday to announce that its Gmail service is actually running just fine. In a post, the company said it was not currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded users they could always check Gmail’s real-time status on its online dashboard . As it turns out, the company was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own . While some posts on the social network suggested Gmail was experiencing a disruption, others said they were not having any problems. The concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where users can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems. Downdetector is not an official source for verifying or understanding the true scope of internet outages, and as people become more concerned about possible cyberattacks, the site’s data may become less valuable over time if every minor glitch and hiccup is reported as an “outage” by non-technical users. The fact that Google had to announce it was not having an outage speaks to the growing anxiety around the reliability of major tech services. items.title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
items.description: Gemini's Task mode can help users coordinate calls, log into websites, and even make purchases on the user's behalf.
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: Google is expanding the rollout of Tasks, a toggle in Gemini that converts the chatbot into a more active helper. Unlike Gemini’s Chat, which merely allows users to talk to Google’s AI assistant for informational purposes, Tasks empowers the app to complete basic secretarial functions, deputizing it as a kind of personal assistant. How, specifically, can you use it? Google says that the app can call businesses and book appointments on users’ behalf; it can also complete purchases for them via Google Pay, and even sign into websites securely if prompted to do so. In a blog post , Josh Woodword, VP of Gemini, claims to have recently used the feature to call local car dealerships to schedule a service appointment for his family’s minivan. He says he also used it to analyze his electrical bill. Tasks was initially launched to select testers back in May as Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agentic helper, and was expanded to U.S. subscribers of its Google AI Ultra tier. Gemini Spark eventually became “Task Mode.” Google is now making the feature available for free to hundreds of millions of people who are using the company’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. Getting the function up and running is easy. Users merely flip a toggle within the app from Chat to Tasks, which enables the feature. Users can also send texts to Gemini or call the app to give it commands.

Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models. items.description: Sqwish Labs has a new wrinkle on the decision model: Train it with your own data to max its capabilities.
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: In October, more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI model router went to decision models, not LLMs — an enormous share of work for a kind of computerized intelligence that was invented only a month earlier. Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model. TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week). However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his company is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately. The action is happening on both ends of the ecosystem: Sqwish , a U.K.-based AI startup behind a decision model called kettei fat, announced a $3 million pre-seed round today. items.content: Delivery supply chains are the lifeblood of contemporary businesses — and a new startup is betting that purpose-built AI agents can make them run a lot more smoothly. On Tuesday, Pedestal AI emerged from stealth with $4.7 million in seed funding. The company’s goal is to use agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable — a plan that’s already brought them together with Fortune 500 companies and some of the largest shipping firms in the world. The seed round was led by Eclipse, with participation from RRE, Converge VC, Timescale Ventures, and VitalStage. Pedestal says the funding will be used to expand its product and engineering time, grow the marketing organization, and support additional deployments. In practice, much of Pedestal’s work is about removing friction from the shipping process — with agentic technology used as a means to that end. In one case, the company reduced missed deliveries for a major furniture company by 20% by deploying agents to take on some of the work that drivers were supposed to do. The agentic system they built would call customers 30 minutes before a delivery and collect any special instructions; if the call didn’t go through, a text would be sent from a separate system. Along the way, the deployment collected a wealth of data about friction points in the process, which could be used to optimize the system even further. items.description: Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. They usually compiled.
items.author: Kirsten Korosec, Rebecca Bellan
items.content: Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals. Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery. The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game. The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence. Earlier this year, Anthropic became embroiled in a dispute with the Department of Defense after it told the agency it could not use Anthropic’s technology for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous warfare. items.title: Daydream’s new AI agent acts as your personal stylist — and can shop for you, too
items.description: Daydream's new AI shopping agent can remember your style, virtually try on clothes, plan outfits around your wardrobe, track sales, and complete purchases.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out. On Tuesday, the company launched “Daydream Agent,” an AI agent that is described as a personal stylist that can help you plan a look, virtually try on clothes, surface relevant pieces based on your taste, and more. The idea, the company explains, is to put a personal stylist in everyone’s pocket. This application of AI could be promising, given that early adopters of consumer AI agents like Meta’s Muse have found that online shopping is a key use case. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently noted that shopping was a top activity for Muse’s over 10 million users and that 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily. In Daydream’s case, the fashion startup has been focused on using AI to deliver personalized shopping results to its users. Its new AI agent builds on its earlier work with an AI chatbot that could help users find outfits and make suggestions, but not complete purchases. Now the company says its Daydream Agent expands on that experience by remembering each shopper’s own personal style, fit preferences, and budget to refine its recommendations. Shoppers can also upload a photo to have the agent reuse that image to virtually try on any item they’ve saved. items.author: Russell Brandom
items.content: Planning a trip is a favorite demo for personal AI assistants — you can try it with Muse, or with Gemini, or half a dozen other choices. But while most pitches use travel-planning as part of a general-purpose agent pitch, a new startup from a Google Maps alum is betting that a specialized travel-planning agent can beat the competition. The company is called Voyage Labs , and on Tuesday it announced $12 million in seed funding led by Kleiner Perkins, with participation from SignalFire and SV Angel. The company plans to use the funding to expand supplier partnerships and grow its engineering team. Voyage Labs’ flagship product, called Atlas, is meant to work as a personal assistant for your trip-planning, available today in private beta . “People can use it to plan and book and manage their entire journey, from the time they have an inspiration to the time they come back home,” says co-founder and CEO Manik Gupta. Atlas is designed to serve as an always-on assistant throughout the planning process, fielding ideas and doing research on every idea that’s raised. The long time horizon means Atlas can tailor recommendations based on weeks of conversation, while also monitoring real-time price fluctuations and ultimately booking flights and hotels. items.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B as it looks to take drug candidates to clinical trials
items.description: Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-discovery platform that was spun out of Google’s DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 billion in a Series C funding round.
items.author: Ram Iyer
items.content: Isomorphic Labs , the AI drug-discovery platform that was spun out of Google’s DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 billion in a Series C funding round as it seeks to take its drug candidates to clinical trials. The funding was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with new investor Andreessen Horowitz and other investors also participating. All of the company’s existing backers, including Alphabet’s venture divisions GV and Capita G, Thrive Capital, MGX, Temasek, and the U.K. Sovereign AI Fund, also invested. Isomorphic Labs builds an AI drug-design engine that uses a slew of simulation AI models that explore various areas of chemistry to help the company design drugs. The company, whose work builds on DeepMind’s breakthrough AlphaFold protein-folding AI model , said its program has yielded “positive preclinical results” in oncology and immunology. The lab has struck deals with pharma giants like Eli Lilly, Novartis, and Johnson & Johnson. The new funding, which comes on the heels of a $2.1 billion Series B round in May, will be used to continue developing its drug-design engine, as well as to foray into more types of medicine. The Series C is Isomorphic’s first fundraise since its founder and CEO, Demis Hassabis, left his position as head of DeepMind to focus on drug discovery, which also saw him moving into a chairman role at DeepMind.
